significance.note: No sigma-style significance figure is stated verbatim in the fetched abstract; only the candidate-event count and expected background are given.

summary.plain: On 21 July 2000 the DONUT collaboration announced at Fermilab what the laboratory called the first direct evidence for the tau neutrino. In 203 neutrino interactions recorded in nuclear emulsion, a decay search found evidence of four tau neutrino interactions against an estimated background of 0.34 events; the abstract adds that this number is consistent with the Standard Model expectation.
summary.technical: DONUT analysed 203 neutrino interactions recorded in nuclear-emulsion targets; a decay search found evidence of four tau neutrino interactions with an estimated background of 0.34 events; the abstract adds 'This number is consistent with the Standard Model expectation' (Phys. Lett. B 504, 218). Fermilab's announcement described this as the first direct evidence for the tau neutrino.

title: Observation of tau neutrino interactions
why_it_matters: Fermilab's announcement calls the tau neutrino the third kind of neutrino known to particle physicists and says earlier experiments had produced indirect evidence; DONUT's four events, in which a neutrino interacts to produce a tau lepton, are described there as the first direct evidence for it.
